mainEntity.name: What should I never let an AI automation do without asking me first?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Keep approval before AI sends messages, publishes content, spends money, signs up for services, or changes important records. Automation is safest when the system prepares a recommendation or draft and you confirm the consequential action.

Run My AI Biz specifically describes human-directed automation, approval checkpoints, secure connections, and restrictions on unsupported claims. A chief-of-staff-style assistant can coordinate work, but it should not silently make business commitments.

Key factors:
- Financial or reputational impact
- Customer-specific context
- Difficulty of reversing the action
- Availability of an audit trail

Use three levels: automatic for low-risk organization, review-required for customer-facing drafts, and owner-only for money, access, contracts, or publication. Keep logs showing the input, output, reviewer, and action taken.

Run My AI Biz supports a controlled approach that preserves owner responsibility while reducing repetitive preparation work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Require approval before sending messages, publishing, spending money, signing up for services, changing records, or making customer-specific commitments. Let AI organize and draft low-risk work automatically, but keep consequential actions owner-controlled.
